info.name: AIVoice
info.description: All HTTP endpoints for the AIVoice voice engine (server/) and dashboard (dashboard/).

request.description:
Confirms the voice engine is running. No auth required.

Expected: 200 { ok: true, service: 'aivoice-voice-engine', phase: 1, provider: 'openai-realtime' }

Returns TwiML XML that connects to /stream with tenantId=1.
This is what Twilio calls when a phone call comes in (diagnostic version hardcoded to tenant 1).

Expected: 200 application/xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Response><Connect><Stream url="wss://…/stream?tenantId=1" /></Connect></Response>

urlencoded.description: The Twilio phone number that was dialed (E.164). Server maps this to a tenant.
Caller's number (Twilio includes this; server ignores it but Twilio always sends it).
Twilio call ID (optional for this test).

request.description:
Simulates Twilio calling your webhook when someone dials your number.
Server parses the 'To' field, looks up the tenant by phone number, then returns TwiML pointing to /stream?tenantId=<id>.

Expected: 200 application/xml with a <Connect><Stream> TwiML response.
If 'To' doesn't match any tenant in DB, falls back to tenantId=1.

WebSocket endpoint. Twilio connects here to stream real-time audio.
Use Postman's WebSocket request type (New → WebSocket) to connect.

URL: ws://localhost:3000/stream?tenantId=1

To simulate the handshake, send these JSON messages in order:

1. Connected event:
{"event":"connected","protocol":"Call","version":"1.0.0"}

2. Start event:
{"event":"start","start":{"streamSid":"MZtest","callSid":"CAtest","tracks":["inbound"]}}

The server will open a connection to OpenAI Realtime and (if OPENAI_API_KEY is set) Sarah will begin speaking.

Note: You will NOT hear audio — media payloads are base64 μ-law and meant for Twilio.

item.name: Dashboard (Next.js)
item.description:
Dashboard runs on port 3001. All routes below require a signed-in NextAuth session.

To authenticate in Postman:
1. Open http://localhost:3001/login in your browser and sign in.
2. Open DevTools → Application → Cookies → copy the value of 'next-auth.session-token'.
3. In Postman, go to the request → Cookies → add a cookie for 'localhost' with name 'next-auth.session-token' and that value.
4. All requests in this folder will then go through as authenticated.
